home.injury_description: Per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard, Oliver notified the Bills' medical staff Saturday morning of pain in his oblique, but there's still optimism that the veteran defensive lineman will be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt. In the event that Oliver is inactive or operates on a snap count, more playing time on defense would be available for DeWayne Carter, Greg Gaines and Landon Jackson.

Alford upgraded his practice participation in each subsequent session of Week 11 prep as he progressed through the five stages of the NFL's concussion protocol. The slot cornerback has been cleared by an independent neurologist and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game.

Kincaid was held out of practice all week while tending to thumb and ankle injuries, and he's trending toward being inactive for Sunday's AFC East tilt. If Kincaid is indeed ruled out, then Knox will operate as the Bills' top tight end, with Jackson Hawes (shoulder) and Keleki Latu also in line for larger roles on offense. Knox has 14 catches (on 20 targets) for 86 yards and a touchdown through nine regular-season games, and the Bills face a Dolphins defense that ranks 25th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.

Hooker was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but the veteran safety was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's AFC East showdown. Hooker made his Bills debut against the Jets in Week 10, when he logged seven tackles (four solo) and one pass defense in a 31-12 win for Buffalo.

Hamlin was held out of practice in each of the first two practices of Week 11 prep due to a toe injury. He put together a limited session Friday to draw the questionable tag, but if he cannot play against the Dolphins, then Jalon Kilgore and Sam Franklin would operate as the Bills' backup safeties behind Amani Hooker and Cole Bishop for Sunday's AFC East tilt.

away.injury_description: Baker opened the season on the Dolphins' PUP list due to a knee injury. He was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, and while he's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills, Baker appears to be in line to make his 2026 regular-season debut. He played in all 17 regular-season games for the Titans in 2025 and finished with 55 tackles (39 solo) and seven pass defenses.

Carlson signed with the Dolphins' practice squad Tuesday, two weeks after being released by the Saints. Following the Dolphins' release of Zane Gonzalez, Carlson will operate as Miami's kicker for Sunday's game against Buffalo. In seven appearances with the Saints this season, Carlson went 8-for-12 on field-goal attempts (including 3-for-7 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 16-for-18 on extra-point tries.

Simpson upgraded to a limited participant in Friday's practice after missing consecutive sessions to start Week 11 prep. The reserve cornerback remains unlikely to suit up, but Friday's partial session gives the 26-year-old a chance to be active on game day.

Pinion did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions. The punter likely sustained his groin injury in the Dolphins' Week 10 loss to the Colts. Jack Browning is set to be elevated from the practice squad ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills to take over punting duties.

Meyer suffered a stinger against the Colts in Week 10, but his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's AFC East game. He would likely start at center for a second consecutive week if Aaron Brewer (concussion) is not cleared to play.

Meanwhile, Monangai turned his 65 touches into 363 total yards and three rushing TDs during that same stretch. Both players figure to be utilized liberally by head coach Ben Johnson in Week 11 and beyond, though Swift is the better weekly bet to surpass 50 percent of the offensive snaps.

Gordon did not participate in practice coming off the Bears' bye week after picking up a shoulder injury in the team's Week 9 game against the Buccaneers. Week 11 marks the sixth game the 26-year-old has missed this season. Malik Muhammad, who is coming back from a toe injury, is expected to see more reps in Gordon's place.

Simmons logged full participation in Friday's practice after beginning the week as limited with a knee injury. Since joining the Bears, the 29-year-old has 10 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass breakups on 119 defensive snaps.

Thomas appears to have picked up an injury in the Bears' lead-up to Week 11, as he did not participate in Friday's practice. The rookie third-rounder acts as the team's top kick-return option. Should he not play, Josh Blackwell may take over duties on special teams.

away.injury_description: Smyth has been elevated from the Saints' practice squad for each of the team's last two games following the release of Daniel Carlson on Nov. 3. Smyth has gone 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 4-for-4 on extra-point tries in his two appearances, and his new deal means he'll be the Saints' kicker through the 2027 season.

Richards suffered a significant knee injury in the Saints' Week 10 loss to the Panthers. The offensive tackle is expected to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, so his absence for Week 11 is no surprise. Mason Murphy is set to start at right tackle while Richards recovers.

McCoy has not practiced since sustaining a biceps injury in the Saints' Week 9 clash with the Browns. The center will now miss consecutive games due to the injury, leaving Cesar Ruiz to start at center against the Bears.
Fuaga did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions due to a knee injury he sustained during Week 10 prep. The right tackle will now miss consecutive games due to the issue.

Emerson was unable to practice all week while in the league's concussion protocol. Corbin last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he appeared in six games as a member of the Giants.

He'll end up missing an eighth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury he picked up in Week 3 against the Ravens. Thompson's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

Bland was expected to miss multiple games due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the 49ers. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Dec. 27. Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant are both in line for larger roles in Dallas' secondary in Bland's absence.

Locke was unable to practice all week while in the league's concussion protocol, and his absence means Markquese Bell will likely start alongside Malik Hooker at safety Sunday. Locke's next chance to play is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

Ezeiruaku didn't play against the 49ers in Week 10 due to an ankle injury. He's avoided an injury tag for Week 11 after logging a full practice Friday, and his return means less rotational snaps at the edge rusher position will be available for James Houston and Von Miller. Ezeiruaku has 32 tackles (16 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.

However, per Rapoport, the wideout -- who last played in Week 7 -- is poised to rejoin the Titans' lineup, with his Week 11 status set to be officially confirmed, either way, before the first wave of games Sunday, with a 1:00 pm ET kickoff on tap.

Harrell is being monitored following Saturday's accident. The third-year pro tore his ACL in a preseason game against the 49ers in mid-August, which led to him being placed on season-ending injured reserve.

Adams logged a full practice Friday to draw the questionable tag, and he's now out of the league's concussion protocol after passing an evaluation from an independent neurologist. The veteran safety has accumulated 35 tackles (20 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

The elevation of Carter gives the Titans extra depth at running back following the placement of Tyjae Spears (knee) on injured reserve. Carter -- who has appeared in three regular-season games for Tennessee -- is listed as the fourth running back on the depth chart behind Tony Pollard, Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton.

Spears was sidelined for Weeks 7 and 8 due to a knee injury but was cleared to play against the Jaguars in Week 10, when he turned four carries into 28 yards and failed to haul in his lone target. He was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys after logging a full practice Friday, but the Titans have determined that a stint on injured reserve is warranted for the fourth-year running back. Spears will be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Colts on Sunday, Dec. 20. Tony Pollard will continue to be the workhorse running back for the Titans while Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton provide depth out of the backfield.

Khalil Dorsey (ankle) and Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) are both also listed as questionable, which leaves Rock Ya-Sin, Roger McCreary and Christian Izien as the only healthy cornerbacks on the Lions' 53-man roster heading into the weekend.

If Vaki is unable to play against Tampa Bay, Jacob Saylors would move up to RB2 status, but Jahmyr Gibbs would have a chance to see an even bigger share of the backfield opportunities in that scenario.

McCreary recorded his first interception of the season in Week 10, when he jumped in front of a pass from Tommy DeVito -- who took over under center for the Patriots after Drake Maye injured his ankle in the first quarter -- that was intended for Mack Hollins, although the Lions' offense couldn't convert the takeaway into points. McCreary is up to 38 tackles (28 solo), including 1.0 sacks, 10 pass defenses and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.

Joseph was a full participant in his return to the active roster Wednesday. The free safety is set to make his 2026 debut in Week 11 against the Buccaneers, finally reuniting with strong safety Brian Branch after both spent lengthy periods on the Lions' reserve lists.

away.injury_description: Mayfield, who has been dealing with a plantar fascia injury in his foot that had him in a walking boot for several days, per the report, was limited in practice Thursday and Friday before approaching the contest listed as questionable. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix previously reported that the QB will wear a special orthotic and new cleats to stabilize his foot as he plays through the injury Sunday, with Jalon Daniels on hand in the event that Mayfield suffers an in-game setback. Official confirmation on Mayfield's Week 11 status is set to arrive once inactives are posted ahead of Tampa Bay's 1:00 pm ET kickoff.

Hayes was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, but he is not quite ready to return from a knee procedure that he underwent in late August. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.

Diaby suffered a Grade 2 MCL sprain during the Buccaneers' Week 8 win over the Falcons, and the injury prevented him from playing against the Bears in Week 9. He had additional time to recover thanks to the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, and he drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game after putting together an LP-LP-FP practice log. Diaby's return would result in less defensive snaps for David Walker and Al-Quadin Muhammad.

Winfield injured his ankle against the Bears in Week 9, and the extra week of rest courtesy of the bye was not enough for him to practice in any capacity during Week 11 prep. Ifeatu Melifonwu will likely start alongside Tykee Smith at safety in the absence of Winfield, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.

Mayfield injured his foot in Week 9 against the Bears and sat out of Wednesday's practice, which resulted in Daniels taking all of the first-team reps during that session. Mayfield returned to practice Thursday and Friday as a limited participant, and it appears as though the 2018 first-overall pick will be under center for Sunday's game, which would result in Daniels operating as the backup and Easton Stick as the emergency third quarterback. Daniels started from Weeks 4 through 6 and went 1-2 over that stretch, when he completed 63.2 percent of his passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions while turning 19 carries into 117 yards.

His return would give the Chiefs more depth on the interior defensive line behind starters Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga.

Moore will miss a second consecutive game due to an ankle injury, which means Joshua Ezeudu will likely start at right tackle against Arizona. Moore's next chance to play is Week 12 against Buffalo on Thanksgiving Day.

Kelce was forced from last Sunday's game against the Falcons with the ankle injury, but he's good to go for Week 11 against a hapless Arizona squad. The Chiefs should run all over the Cardinals defense and likely won't need much pass volume from Patrick Mahomes. Kelce is more of a fringe TE1 for fantasy purposes.

The veteran wideout played seven offensive snaps in Arizona's loss to the Rams last Sunday. With a boatload of injuries at the position, Jones figures to have a role for the foreseeable future. He has no fantasy appeal in this injury-ruined offense.

The Cardinals were already preparing for Josh Johnson to operate as the starting quarterback Sunday, as Beck entered the weekend with the questionable tag due to back spasms. He appears to be closing in on his first game action since Week 5, when he suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia, but his status for Sunday's matchup won't be confirmed until about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Assuming Shipley returns to action this weekend, he may serve as the direct backup to top RB Saquon Barkley.

Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

Jones logged a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury designation and return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. He's contributed both on defense and special teams and has six tackles (five solo) and one pass defense across seven regular-season games.

An abdominal injury prevented Carter from playing in Week 9 against the Giants. He had extra rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. Carter's return gives the Eagles a boost in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.

Barring an unannounced setback, Pittman figures to continue practicing, and his next chance to take the field will arrive Black Friday, when the Steelers square off against the Broncos.

He's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, but his activation from IR indicates that the third-year wide receiver will suit up for the Steelers. Michael Pittman (foot) is staying on IR for at least one more week, so as it stands, Wilson slots in as the team's WR3 behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.

Watt. Herbig's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Broncos on Friday.

Hawkins was a limited participant throughout the practice week, but it isn't enough for him to return in Week 11. The 29-year-old will miss his fifth straight game due to a knee injury. K'Von Wallace will continue to take reps in Hawkins' place.

Madubuike popped up on the injury report as a non-participant in back-to-back practices due to a hamstring injury. With the 29-year-old out, John Jenkins will likely see a higher snap count on defense. Madubuike has 22 tackles (12 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass deflections in eight regular-season games.

Per Hensley, Humphrey acknowledged after Wednesday's practice that he regretted the comments he made in the podcast and issued an apology, so he's not expected to face any discipline beyond being held out of the matchup with the Panthers. Through the Ravens' first 10 games, Humphrey has tallied 40 tackles, nine pass breakups, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.

If he's let go by the Chargers, then Dupree could garner interest from teams looking for a boost in the pass rush.

Waxter ended Week 11 prep with consecutive limited sessions after being a non-participant Wednesday. If Waxter cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Deane Leonard is set to be the only reserve cornerback behind starters Cam Hart, Donte Jackson and Tarheeb Still (ankle).

Parham practiced in all three Week 11 prep sessions, logging consecutive limited practices before upgrading to a full participant Friday. Despite the upgrade to full participation, the offensive guard remains questionable for Sunday's contest, meaning his knee is likely still bothering him.

Runyon appeared in 13 games with the Raiders last season but logged just 45 offensive snaps and caught only one pass for three yards. He's depth behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas.
